title.narrative: Support to Refugee Response to New Arrivals in Kiryandongo District, Uganda.

description.narrative: A GBP 5,000,000 award addressing the new arrivals from Sudan. Since December 2023, Kiryandongo settlement has seen a significant influx of new arrivals primarily from Sudan due to the ongoing civil conflict in the country. This is driving an increasingly critical humanitarian situation in Kiryandongo, with 20% of the settlementâ€™s population currently facing acute food insecurity and a further 30% at risk.

GeographicalThe programme will operate in Kiryandongo due to:Growing demand for humanitarian support within the settlement due to the rapid influx of primarily Sudanese refugees since the settlement was reopened. The programme will not be geographically targeted within the settlement.GiveDirectly has a longstanding presence in Kiryandongo settlement, and has a proven track record of delivering cash there safely and efficiently. This gives us a strong comparative advantage to respond quickly, effectively and with the trust of the community and government.

This intervention aims to achieve the following objectives:(A.) Empower refugees:Large cash grants can empower refugees to establish new businesses, pursue professional recertification, continue their careers, or seek other livelihood opportunities, fostering economic independence and contributing to the local economy. In Uganda, the cost to translate and equate foreign academic documents for refugees costs around 250,000 UGX ($68) per education certificate.(B.) Ease pressures on the existing refugee population:By providing substantial financial support to the newly arrived refugees, we can enable them to quickly pursue self-reliance, reducing the burden on shared resources available to the existing refugee population. Additionally, empowering highly skilled and educated refugees, who are capable of quickly setting up enterprises, can lead to job creation - positively impacting the broader community.(C.) Protect gains from previous livelihoods investments:This intervention will protect the gains made from GiveDirectly and other livelihood investments in the settlement. By addressing the needs of new arrivals, we can ensure that the progress achieved through earlier cash transfers is not lost, community tensions are not exacerbated and that the community continues on its path to self-reliance.(D.) Enhance local economies:Studies have shown that cash transfers can lead to substantial local economic multiplier effects, benefitting non-recipients. Additionally, there is evidence of broader positive spillover effects including a reduction in intimate partner violence in both recipient and neighboring non-recipient communities, highlighting the broader social benefits of the intervention.
